title: Graded Nakayama generation
statement: Let k be a field and S=k[x_0,x_1] with total-degree grading S_d equal to the k-span of monomials of degree d and S_d=0 for d<0 [def-sc-p1-standard]. Let S_+=(x_0,x_1). If N is a finitely generated Z-graded S-module and homogeneous elements n_1,...,n_r have images generating N/S_+N as a k-vector space, then n_1,...,n_r generate N as an S-module. In particular, if N/S_+N=0, then N=0.

source.place: proof, graded Nakayama criterion applied to K_2

proof.text: Let Q be the graded S-submodule generated by the homogeneous elements n_1,...,n_r and put M=N/Q. Since their classes generate N/S_+N, one has M/S_+M=0, equivalently M=S_+M. The quotient M is finitely generated and graded. By [lem-sc-p1-finite-homogeneous-generators], choose finitely many homogeneous generators m_1,...,m_s of M. Since S has no negative-degree part, every homogeneous element of M has degree at least d=min_j deg(m_j) (unless M=0).

source.place: proof: the graded free resolution quoted from the graded Hilbert syzygy theorem (the blueprint proof does not spell out the graded Nakayama step; the argument here is the agent's own, standard minimal-degree argument)

proof.text: If M were nonzero, choose a nonzero homogeneous y of minimal degree e. The equality M=S_+M and S_+=(x_0,x_1) express y as x_0a+x_1b; taking the degree-e components of a and b gives homogeneous a',b' of degree e-1 with y=x_0a'+x_1b'. This contradicts the minimality of e, since a' or b' would be a nonzero homogeneous element of smaller degree. Thus M=0.

proof.text: Because M=N/Q is zero, N=Q, so the given homogeneous elements n_1,...,n_r generate N as an S-module.
